blockers.quote: One loophole is left open for the comments: the counter resets at midnight, and the debate ended at ten to.
blockers.why: Check #21 fails: the leader can stall ten minutes and erase the climax's count.
blockers.fix: Set the debate at eight and show its clock; give the leader thirty seconds to read or forfeit his final response. Remove the sentence leaving this loophole open.

blockers.quote: By tonight you'll know the number over every head in this city. Every head but one.
blockers.why: Check #3 fails: by 0:30 the blind spot is clear, but the concrete gain and risk are not.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "By tonight, nobody can fool you. But you can't see your own—and everyone will ask."

blockers.quote: about sixty percent reported no lies in the past day, and about half of all lies came from about five percent of people; the average, near one and a half to two, is pulled up by a few
blockers.why: Check #7 fails: several numbers arrive together instead of one belief-breaking number landing through the scene.
blockers.fix: Keep only: "In one U.S. survey, about sixty percent reported no lies the previous day." Show the bus zeros, then cut to the boss's 47 and say: "A tiny group told most of the rest."

suggestions.fix: Make reading unavoidable: the host says, "If it's true, reading costs you nothing," the opponent repeats the challenge, and refusal now costs him the debate; therefore he reads.

suggestions.quote: So, would you want to see the number over your own head? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Use one closing question after "Nine?": "Would you still want to see yours?" Then cut.

keep.quote: The city isn't lying to you. The city is mostly fine. The five percent has a corner office.
Read it out loud. For the people who can't see.
